claim: Ads promoting lower-carbon offerings (100% renewable electricity, offshore wind, EV charging)
reason: The ads implied lower-carbon products made up a significant share of Shell's business, when oil and gas investment and extraction were the vast majority. That proportion was material information the ads left out.

claim: “Green Diesel” … “helps protect the environment” … emissions cut “up to 40%”
reason: Environmental benefits of the HVO component were attributed to the whole diesel product, a fuel that is highly polluting by nature. The performance figures were partial or lacked context.

claim: Vague sustainability claims and statements about SAF and reforestation (15 of 19 statements challenged)
reason: The court found the claims rested on vague, general statements of environmental benefit and painted too rosy a picture of measures that only marginally reduce harm.

claim: “Explore the World With Confidence and Total Peace Of Mind With Etihad Airways. Environmental Advocacy.”
reason: An absolute environmental claim with no evidence of advocacy. Air travel produces high CO2 and non-CO2 emissions. Breached CAP Code 3.1, 11.1 and 11.3.

claim: Representations that diesel vehicles complied with Australian emissions standards (incl. Green Vehicle Guide listings)
reason: VW did not disclose ‘two mode’ software that changed engine behaviour during testing. Note: this is emissions-compliance deception rather than a marketing slogan.

claim: “Conscious” collection labels and product sustainability claims
reason: The ACM found the sustainability claims insufficiently clear and specific. H&M agreed to remove or adjust them. Note: this was a negotiated commitment decision, not a court finding of breach.

claim: “Little drinks with big dreams for a healthier planet”
reason: The ads implied buying Innocent benefits the environment. There was no evidence of a net positive impact over the full lifecycle, and the bottles contain non-recycled plastic.

claim: “…up to $1 trillion in financing and investment globally to help…clients transition to net zero”; “helping to plant 2 million trees”
reason: Accurate in isolation, but the ads left out that HSBC continued to significantly finance high-emitting industries.

claim: “Die Apple Watch ist unser erstes CO2 neutrales Produkt” (“Apple Watch is our first CO2-neutral product”)
reason: Misleading under UWG §5: the offset projects were not secured long enough to support a CO2-neutral claim. The ‘Carbon Neutral’ logo itself was not found misleading. Open to appeal.
Unclear what the comparison was against, and no full-lifecycle evidence supported it.
